First brick: knowledge.

What it knows about you.

Nice. Generic. It has never met us. “Tell me the kids’ ages and your budget.”

Claude Sonnet 5.5, incognito chat (no memory), 17 Nov 2026

Same question, asked three times.

Context makes it consistent.

I built a knowledge base and connected it to an agent. Same question: now it knows us.

A knowledge base fills the gap.

Retraining a model is slow and expensive. A knowledge base you can update tonight.

Why not give it everything? The desk is small.

The desk = what the AI can see at once. It grows every year, but it never holds everything.

Clean, relevant data makes agents fast and cheap.

Liu et al., “Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts”, 2023 (TACL 2024)

My second brain · 1 of 3

I started small: a few notes.

Easy to write. Hard to find.

My second brain · 2 of 3

Then I sorted them into folders myself.

Tidy for a week. Then messy again.

My second brain · 3 of 3

Karpathy’s idea: let AI keep the notes.

I drop things in. AI files, tags and links them.

Andrej Karpathy, “LLM Wiki” (GitHub gist) · plain notes in a folder I own, so any AI can read them

The advanced option · for lots of documents

RAG: an open-book test.

RAG = look it up first, then answer. For thousands of files. Understand it before you build it.

★ Try it yourself

Build yours: simple to complex.

Start simple. Start tonight.

It knows us. But it can’t check a flight.

No tools. Second brick: what it can do.

Some things can’t live in a knowledge base.

API = a system’s own way to ask it for things.

Why not connect each API directly?

Every API speaks its own language. Without a standard, every agent needs its own code for every tool. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is that standard.

MCP is like Bluetooth, for AI.

A standard your AI apps already support. Connect, approve, done. No code.

Level 2 · AI uses my tools

Now it can check, not guess.

★ Try it yourself

Your first connection: the calendar.

No code. It can look, not change.

Third brick: skills.

Make it work the way you work.

Every time I ask, it agrees.

It agrees every time. Even when I’m wrong.

And every new chat starts empty.

It only knows what’s in this chat. So you repeat yourself. Every time.

A skill: a friend’s know-how, built in.

Write it once. Ask for it by name.

Memory = facts about you. A skill = how to do a job.
Where it lives: Skills in Claude · custom GPTs in ChatGPT · agents in Copilot

My favourite skill

grill-me: it doesn’t agree. It asks.

A skill that builds skills

50 emails → my writing style.

Now every draft sounds like me.

Thousands are free. Borrow one, make it yours.

github.com/anthropics/skills · github.com/obra/superpowers · Matt Pocock’s skills

★ Try it yourself

Which of your skills would you write down for AI?

Write it down once. Connect it to your agent. Then it acts like you, for you.

Challenge 3: AI at scale for enterprises.

Five rooms, five doors, everything built five times. There has to be one way in.

The answer: one front door for AI.

Its name at work: an AI gateway.

Behind the door: one playbook, every agent.

Written once. Used by every agent.
